Texas publishes no statewide expunction form at any level of state government, so nothing gets rejected for being the wrong form; what varies across the 254 counties is formatting practice — civil cover sheets, how sensitive data is handled, how a hearing is set, how many copies, and whether the clerk or the filer prepares the notice of hearing. The first call is to the district clerk of that county, asking by name for the list of agencies and e-mail addresses that art. 55A.253(c) requires the clerk to publish on the clerk's website. Before that, the clerk of the court that dismissed the charge is where the dismissal order comes from.
destination.es: La petición ex parte se presenta en un tribunal de distrito del condado donde a usted lo arrestaron o donde se alegó que ocurrió el delito, conforme al art. 55A.251, y no en el condado donde vive. Si el arresto fue por un delito sancionable únicamente con multa, el art. 55A.252 también permite un tribunal de paz o un tribunal municipal de registro en cualquiera de los dos condados. El asunto es una acción civil nueva y recibe un número de causa nuevo. Texas no publica ningún formulario estatal de expunción en ningún nivel del gobierno, así que nada se rechaza por ser el formulario equivocado; lo que cambia entre los 254 condados es la práctica de formato: carátulas civiles, manejo de datos sensibles, cómo se fija la audiencia, cuántas copias y si la notificación de audiencia la prepara el secretario o quien presenta. La primera llamada es al secretario del tribunal de distrito de ese condado, pidiendo por su nombre la lista de organismos y correos electrónicos que el art. 55A.253(c) obliga al secretario a publicar en el sitio web de la secretaría. Antes de eso, el secretario del tribunal que sobreseyó el cargo es de donde sale la orden de sobreseimiento.

timing.en: There is no waiting period stated in art. 55A.053, and under art. 55A.053(d) entitlement does not depend on any limitations period — so waiting is not what this route asks of you. The timing rule that does bite comes after filing: the hearing is set not earlier than the 30th day following the date the petition is filed, and the court gives a copy of the petition and the notice of hearing to each listed official, agency and entity other than the central federal depositories; DPS notifies those depositories on receipt. One timing trap is worth knowing: where entitlement would otherwise rest on the expiry of an art. 55A.052(a)(1) to (3) period without a prosecutor's certification, art. 55A.302(c) requires records retention — so waiting for a limitations period to run can change what you actually end up with, turning a full expunction into a partial one.
timing.es: El art. 55A.053 no establece ningún período de espera, y conforme al art. 55A.053(d) el derecho no depende de ningún plazo de prescripción, así que esperar no es lo que esta vía le pide. La regla de tiempo que sí pesa llega después de presentar: la audiencia se fija no antes del día 30 siguiente a la fecha de presentación de la petición, y el tribunal entrega copia de la petición y de la notificación de audiencia a cada funcionario, organismo y entidad de la lista, salvo los depositarios federales centrales; el DPS avisa a esos depositarios al recibirla. Vale la pena conocer una trampa de tiempo: cuando el derecho descansaría por lo demás en el vencimiento de un plazo del art. 55A.052(a)(1) a (3) sin certificación del fiscal, el art. 55A.302(c) exige la retención de registros, de modo que esperar a que corra un plazo de prescripción puede cambiar lo que finalmente obtiene, convirtiendo una expunción total en una parcial.

stopReason.en: Nothing is being prepared or sold for this route yet, and the reasons are specific. The Texas legal review that governs this route leaves three questions open that it marks as blocking release, and every one of them is about what you would be handed or what it would cost you. First, nobody can currently tell you what filing this costs in your county. The old expunction fee statute, art. 102.006, was repealed effective 1 September 2025, temporarily re-added with a built-in expiry, and permanently replaced by art. 102.0061 effective 1 January 2026. Under art. 102.0061(a) a district court charges the fee applicable to filing an ex parte petition in a civil action in district court — the ordinary county civil filing fee, which is not a flat statutory amount and differs from county to county; under (b) a justice court or municipal court of record charges a flat $100. Which provision governs is settled; the county figure is not, and the old $250-to-$500 range still circulating is no longer reliable and is not quoted to you. Second, on top of the filing fee, art. 55A.254(e) forbids the clerk charging anything to transmit the petition or notice of hearing electronically, while art. 55A.254(f) requires the clerk to charge $25 for each listed entity that cannot receive an electronic transmission, and the same structure repeats at the order stage under art. 55A.351(b-2) and (b-3). Whether the same paper-only agency is charged twice, once at each stage, follows from the statutory text but is unconfirmed in practice — and it multiplies by the number of agencies you list. Third, and this one is about your privacy rather than your wallet: art. 55A.253 requires your social security number and date of birth to appear in the petition, and the petition is a public civil filing until the order issues. How the largest counties — Harris, Dallas, Bexar, Tarrant and Travis — actually handle sensitive data in that filing has not been established, and putting your social security number into a public document on a formatting guess is not something we will do to you. Separately from all three, this route has two hard stops that are not about our readiness and will not change: a dismissal order that does not state one of the five art. 55A.053(a)(2) grounds establishes no ground, and we do not write that a dismissal was for want of probable cause where the order does not say so; and a completed deferred adjudication that ended in discharge and dismissal is not a dismissal for these purposes, except for certain Class C matters, so it is not filed on this basis. Everything above about the mechanism, the destination and what to gather is settled and is yours to act on today.
stopReason.es: Todavía no se prepara ni se vende nada para esta vía, y los motivos son concretos. La revisión legal de Texas que rige esta vía deja abiertas tres preguntas que marca como impedimentos para su publicación, y todas ellas son sobre qué se le entregaría o cuánto le costaría. Primero: hoy nadie puede decirle cuánto cuesta presentar esto en su condado. La antigua ley de tarifas de expunción, el art. 102.006, fue derogada con efecto al 1 de septiembre de 2025, reincorporada de forma temporal con vencimiento incorporado, y sustituida de forma permanente por el art. 102.0061 con efecto al 1 de enero de 2026. Conforme al art. 102.0061(a), un tribunal de distrito cobra la tarifa que corresponde a presentar una petición ex parte en una acción civil en ese tribunal, es decir la tarifa civil ordinaria del condado, que no es un monto fijo de ley y varía de condado a condado; conforme al inciso (b), un tribunal de paz o municipal de registro cobra $100 fijos. Cuál disposición rige ya está resuelto; la cifra del condado no, y el viejo rango de $250 a $500 que todavía circula ya no es confiable y no se lo citamos. Segundo: además de la tarifa de presentación, el art. 55A.254(e) prohíbe que el secretario cobre algo por transmitir electrónicamente la petición o la notificación de audiencia, mientras que el art. 55A.254(f) le exige cobrar $25 por cada entidad de la lista que no pueda recibir una transmisión electrónica, y la misma estructura se repite en la etapa de la orden conforme al art. 55A.351(b-2) y (b-3). Si a un mismo organismo que solo recibe papel se le cobra dos veces, una en cada etapa, se desprende del texto legal pero no está confirmado en la práctica, y se multiplica por la cantidad de organismos que usted enumere. Tercero, y este es sobre su privacidad y no sobre su bolsillo: el art. 55A.253 exige que su número de seguro social y su fecha de nacimiento aparezcan en la petición, y la petición es una presentación civil pública hasta que se dicte la orden. Cómo manejan realmente los condados más grandes — Harris, Dallas, Bexar, Tarrant y Travis — los datos sensibles en esa presentación no está establecido, y poner su número de seguro social en un documento público basándonos en una suposición de formato no es algo que le vayamos a hacer. Aparte de esos tres puntos, esta vía tiene dos altos definitivos que no dependen de si estamos listos y que no van a cambiar: una orden de sobreseimiento que no enuncia uno de los cinco motivos del art. 55A.053(a)(2) no acredita ningún motivo, y nosotros no escribimos que un sobreseimiento fue por falta de causa probable cuando la orden no lo dice; y una adjudicación diferida completada que terminó en liberación y sobreseimiento no es un sobreseimiento para estos efectos, salvo en ciertos asuntos de Clase C, así que no se presenta sobre esa base. Todo lo anterior sobre el mecanismo, el destino y lo que hay que reunir está firme y usted puede actuar hoy con ello.

afterNextStep.en: Once you have the dismissal orders in hand, one of three things is true. If an order names one of the five grounds, that is what a petition would rest on and the order is attached to it — the next work is the art. 55A.253 information set and the agency list, which is where the district clerk's published art. 55A.253(c) list comes in. If the ground is a veterans treatment court or mental health court program, you also answer whether you have had an expunction on that ground before, because each is available once only and an affidavit attesting to that goes with the petition. If the order says only "dismissed", the question becomes whether the dismissing court's file shows the reason, and that is a question for the clerk of that court and then for a Texas record-clearing attorney — not a gap to be papered over with a plausible-sounding allegation. And if what you actually completed was deferred adjudication, this is not your route, whatever the paperwork calls the ending, except for certain Class C matters; the Texas materials we rely on treat that as a hard stop here, and it is the most common misrouting in the state, so it is worth being sure. Whatever happens, your DPS criminal history is how you see what agencies are still holding, both before and after.
afterNextStep.es: Cuando tenga las órdenes de sobreseimiento en la mano, será cierta una de tres cosas. Si una orden nombra uno de los cinco motivos, eso es sobre lo que descansaría una petición y esa orden se le adjunta; el trabajo siguiente es el conjunto de información del art. 55A.253 y la lista de organismos, y ahí entra la lista publicada por el secretario conforme al art. 55A.253(c). Si el motivo es un programa de tribunal de veteranos o de salud mental, además debe responder si ya tuvo antes una expunción por ese motivo, porque cada una está disponible una sola vez y con la petición va una declaración jurada que lo acredita. Si la orden solo dice "sobreseído", la pregunta pasa a ser si el expediente del tribunal que sobreseyó muestra el motivo, y esa es una pregunta para el secretario de ese tribunal y luego para un abogado de limpieza de antecedentes de Texas, no un hueco que se tape con una alegación que suene verosímil. Y si lo que usted realmente completó fue una adjudicación diferida, esta no es su vía, sin importar cómo llamen los papeles al desenlace, salvo en ciertos asuntos de Clase C; los materiales de Texas en los que nos basamos lo tratan aquí como un alto definitivo, y es el error de ruta más común del estado, así que conviene asegurarse. Pase lo que pase, su historial penal del DPS es la forma de ver qué organismos siguen teniendo registros, antes y después.

en: These next steps, so you can return to them.
The exact wording of the dismissal order for each charge, and which of the five art. 55A.053(a)(2) grounds it does or does not name.

Your answers on the specialty-court grounds: veterans treatment court under Chapter 124, mental health court under Chapter 125, or a pretrial intervention program authorized under Government Code 76.011 rather than an informal county program — and whether you have had an expunction on either specialty ground before.
Your answer on deferred adjudication, which is not a dismissal for these purposes except for certain Class C matters.

The screening answers: a felony from the same incident, court-ordered community supervision other than for a Class C misdemeanor, an arrest on a probation-violation warrant, and any failure to appear or leaving the jurisdiction after release on bond.
The counties of arrest and of the alleged offense, and whether they differ.
Whether you have obtained your DPS criminal history and the TRN from it, and whether you have asked the district clerk for the art. 55A.253(c) agency and e-mail list.

The exact reason no filing is being prepared for you yet: the county filing figure under art. 102.0061(a) is not established, whether the $25 paper-only agency charge applies twice is unconfirmed, and how the largest counties handle the social security number and date of birth in a public filing has not been established.
es: Estos próximos pasos, para que pueda volver a ellos.
La redacción exacta de la orden de sobreseimiento de cada cargo, y cuál de los cinco motivos del art. 55A.053(a)(2) nombra o no nombra.

Sus respuestas sobre los motivos de tribunales especializados: tribunal de tratamiento para veteranos conforme al Capítulo 124, tribunal de salud mental conforme al Capítulo 125, o un programa de intervención previa al juicio autorizado conforme al art. 76.011 del Código de Gobierno y no un programa informal del condado; y si ya tuvo antes una expunción por cualquiera de esos dos motivos.
Su respuesta sobre la adjudicación diferida, que no es un sobreseimiento para estos efectos salvo en ciertos asuntos de Clase C.

Las respuestas de filtro: un delito grave del mismo hecho, supervisión comunitaria ordenada por el tribunal fuera de un delito menor de Clase C, un arresto con orden por violar la libertad condicional, y cualquier incomparecencia o salida de la jurisdicción tras salir bajo fianza.
Los condados del arresto y del delito alegado, y si son distintos.
Si ya obtuvo su historial penal del DPS y el TRN que aparece en él, y si ya le pidió al secretario del tribunal de distrito la lista de organismos y correos del art. 55A.253(c).

El motivo exacto por el que todavía no se le prepara ninguna presentación: la cifra de presentación del condado conforme al art. 102.0061(a) no está establecida, no está confirmado si el cargo de $25 por organismo que solo recibe papel se aplica dos veces, y no está establecido cómo manejan los condados más grandes el número de seguro social y la fecha de nacimiento en una presentación pública.

handoff.en: Some of this route is not self-help at all, and it is better to know which parts before you start. Take the matter to a Texas record-clearing attorney or a legal aid office where any of these is true: the dismissal order does not state a reason on its face, because nobody should write in a ground the order does not support; you completed deferred adjudication rather than receiving a dismissal; you are not sure whether a pretrial diversion program was authorized under Government Code 76.011 or was an informal county program, because that difference decides the ground; the state opposes the petition or asks the court to retain records under art. 55A.302; one arrest produced several charges that ended differently, since State v. T.S.N. and Ex parte R.P.G.P. govern whether individual offenses from one arrest can be cleared separately and that reasoning is not automated; a felony arose from the same transaction, which can defeat the petition; the applicable limitations period is contested, or you want a full rather than a partial expunction and the limitations analysis is not clear; there is any history of failing to appear or leaving the jurisdiction after release on bond, since art. 55A.154 makes an intentional or knowing absconder ineligible under arts. 55A.052(a)(1) to (3) and 55A.054; the arrest may have been made on a community-supervision violation warrant under art. 42A.751(b), which art. 55A.153 bars; or the arrest and the alleged offense happened in different counties and you cannot tell where to file. If you have any immigration matter — pending, expected or possible — take that to an immigration attorney before using any Texas record-clearing route. And if the goal is to attack the underlying case rather than clear the record, that is a different kind of case entirely and belongs with a criminal defense lawyer. On costs: the Statement of Inability to Afford Payment of Court Costs under Tex. R. Civ. P. 145 is filed with the petition, the Supreme Court of Texas approved a bilingual statewide version in Misc. Docket No. 22-9090, and Rule 145 requires the clerk to make it available without charge and without your asking; art. 102.0061(d) separately requires waiver of the district-court fee where entitlement arises under art. 55A.053(a)(2)(A) or (B).
handoff.es: Parte de esta vía no es autoayuda en absoluto, y conviene saber cuáles partes antes de empezar. Lleve el asunto a un abogado de limpieza de antecedentes de Texas o a una oficina de asistencia legal gratuita si ocurre cualquiera de estas cosas: la orden de sobreseimiento no expresa un motivo en su texto, porque nadie debería inventar un motivo que la orden no respalda; usted completó una adjudicación diferida en lugar de recibir un sobreseimiento; no está seguro de si un programa de desvío previo al juicio estaba autorizado conforme al art. 76.011 del Código de Gobierno o era un programa informal del condado, porque esa diferencia define el motivo; el estado se opone a la petición o pide al tribunal retener registros conforme al art. 55A.302; de un mismo arresto salieron varios cargos que terminaron distinto, ya que State v. T.S.N. y Ex parte R.P.G.P. rigen si los delitos de un mismo arresto pueden borrarse por separado y ese razonamiento no está automatizado; surgió un delito grave del mismo hecho, lo que puede tumbar la petición; el plazo de prescripción aplicable está en disputa, o usted quiere una expunción total y no parcial y el análisis de prescripción no está claro; existe algún antecedente de no comparecer o de irse de la jurisdicción tras salir bajo fianza, ya que el art. 55A.154 vuelve inelegible a quien se fuga de forma intencional o consciente conforme a los arts. 55A.052(a)(1) a (3) y 55A.054; el arresto pudo haberse hecho con una orden por violar la supervisión comunitaria conforme al art. 42A.751(b), lo cual prohíbe el art. 55A.153; o el arresto y el delito alegado ocurrieron en condados distintos y usted no sabe dónde presentar. Si tiene algún asunto migratorio — pendiente, previsto o posible —, llévelo a un abogado de inmigración antes de usar cualquier vía de limpieza de antecedentes de Texas. Y si lo que busca es atacar el caso penal de fondo y no limpiar el expediente, ese es otro tipo de caso por completo y le corresponde a un abogado penalista. Sobre costos: la Declaración de Incapacidad para Pagar Costas Judiciales conforme a la Regla 145 de Procedimiento Civil de Texas se presenta junto con la petición, la Corte Suprema de Texas aprobó una versión bilingüe para todo el estado en el Misc. Docket No. 22-9090, y la Regla 145 obliga al secretario a ponerla a disposición sin costo y sin que usted la pida; además, el art. 102.0061(d) exige exonerar la tarifa del tribunal de distrito cuando el derecho surge conforme al art. 55A.053(a)(2)(A) o (B).

en: Ask the clerk of the court that dismissed the charge for a copy of the order of dismissal for every charge, and read exactly what it says about why. Under art. 55A.053(a)(2) the court has to find one of five reasons — a completed veterans treatment court program under Government Code Chapter 124, a completed mental health court program under Chapter 125, a completed pretrial intervention program authorized under Government Code 76.011, a presentment made because of mistake, false information or another similar reason indicating absence of probable cause at the time of dismissal, or a void charging instrument. The word "dismissed" alone is not one of them.

If the ground would be the veterans treatment court or the mental health court program, check whether you have ever had an expunction on that same ground before. Each is available once only, and art. 55A.053(b) and (c) require an affidavit attesting that you have not.

Settle the deferred adjudication question before anything else. If your case ended with you completing deferred adjudication and receiving a discharge and dismissal, that is not a dismissal for this route except for certain Class C matters, and it is the single most common wrong turn in Texas record clearing.

Request your Texas DPS criminal history by following DPS form CR-63 — fingerprinting through the DPS FAST vendor at $10 plus a $15 record fee, or the hard-card mail route. It carries the TRN that art. 55A.301 requires on the order, and it shows you which agencies hold the arrest. Note that DPS states it may oppose an expunction petition and that its legal staff cannot assist with one.

Call the district clerk of the county where you were arrested, or where the offense was alleged to have happened, and ask by name for the art. 55A.253(c) list of agencies with e-mail addresses. Every e-mail address is free to serve, while each entity that can only receive paper costs $25 under art. 55A.254(f) and again at the order stage under art. 55A.351(b-3), so the list is a direct cost to you. Keep any background-check company on a separate list — art. 55A.253(a)(8)(C) never merges private compilers into the agency list.

Ask that same clerk two more things: what filing an ex parte petition costs in that county today, since art. 102.0061(a) makes it the ordinary district-court civil filing fee rather than a flat statewide amount; and how that county wants the social security number and date of birth that art. 55A.253 requires to be handled, given the petition is public until the order issues.

Write down the screening answers now, because each one can stop the route: a felony from the same incident, court-ordered community supervision other than for a Class C misdemeanor, an arrest made on a probation-violation warrant, and any failure to appear or leaving the jurisdiction after release on bond. If any of those is a yes, take it to a Texas record-clearing attorney or a legal aid office along with the dismissal order.
es: Pídale al secretario del tribunal que sobreseyó el cargo una copia de la orden de sobreseimiento de cada cargo, y lea exactamente qué dice sobre el porqué. Conforme al art. 55A.053(a)(2) el tribunal debe determinar uno de cinco motivos: un programa de tribunal de tratamiento para veteranos completado conforme al Capítulo 124 del Código de Gobierno, un programa de tribunal de salud mental completado conforme al Capítulo 125, un programa de intervención previa al juicio completado y autorizado conforme al art. 76.011 del Código de Gobierno, una presentación hecha por error, información falsa u otro motivo similar que indique ausencia de causa probable al momento del sobreseimiento, o un documento de imputación nulo. La palabra "sobreseído" por sí sola no es ninguno de ellos.

Si el motivo sería el programa del tribunal de veteranos o el del tribunal de salud mental, verifique si alguna vez tuvo antes una expunción por ese mismo motivo. Cada una está disponible una sola vez, y el art. 55A.053(b) y (c) exigen una declaración jurada de que no la ha tenido.

Resuelva antes que nada la pregunta de la adjudicación diferida. Si su caso terminó con usted completando una adjudicación diferida y recibiendo una liberación y sobreseimiento, eso no es un sobreseimiento para esta vía salvo en ciertos asuntos de Clase C, y es el error de ruta más común en la limpieza de antecedentes en Texas.

Solicite su historial penal del DPS de Texas siguiendo el formulario CR-63 del DPS: toma de huellas con el proveedor FAST del DPS por $10 más $15 por el expediente, o la vía de tarjeta física por correo. Trae el TRN que el art. 55A.301 exige en la orden y le muestra qué organismos tienen el arresto. Tenga en cuenta que el DPS declara que puede oponerse a una petición de expunción y que su personal jurídico no puede ayudarle con ella.

Llame al secretario del tribunal de distrito del condado donde lo arrestaron, o donde se alegó que ocurrió el delito, y pídale por su nombre la lista de organismos con correos electrónicos del art. 55A.253(c). Cada correo electrónico se notifica gratis, mientras que cada entidad que solo puede recibir papel cuesta $25 conforme al art. 55A.254(f) y otra vez en la etapa de la orden conforme al art. 55A.351(b-3), así que esa lista es un costo directo para usted. Mantenga a cualquier empresa de verificación de antecedentes en una lista aparte: el art. 55A.253(a)(8)(C) nunca mezcla a los recopiladores privados con la lista de organismos.

Pregúntele a ese mismo secretario dos cosas más: cuánto cuesta hoy presentar una petición ex parte en ese condado, ya que el art. 102.0061(a) la fija en la tarifa civil ordinaria del tribunal de distrito y no en un monto fijo para todo el estado; y cómo quiere ese condado que se maneje el número de seguro social y la fecha de nacimiento que exige el art. 55A.253, dado que la petición es pública hasta que se dicte la orden.

Anote ahora las respuestas de filtro, porque cada una puede detener la vía: un delito grave del mismo hecho, supervisión comunitaria ordenada por el tribunal fuera de un delito menor de Clase C, un arresto hecho con orden por violar la libertad condicional, y cualquier incomparecencia o salida de la jurisdicción tras salir bajo fianza. Si alguna de ellas es un sí, llévela a un abogado de limpieza de antecedentes de Texas o a una oficina de asistencia legal gratuita junto con la orden de sobreseimiento.

authority.citation: Tex. Code Crim. Proc. arts. 55A.051 and 55A.053 — where an indictment or information was presented and then dismissed or quashed, expunction is available if the court finds the dismissal or quashal was because the person completed a veterans treatment court programme under Government Code Chapter 124, completed a mental health court programme under Chapter 125, completed a pretrial intervention programme authorised under Government Code 76.011, the presentment was made because of mistake, false information or another similar reason indicating absence of probable cause at the time of dismissal, or the charging instrument was void (art. 55A.053(a)(2)). Relief is mandatory on the findings, but the court must make the finding about why the case was dismissed.
Tex. Code Crim. Proc. art. 55A.053(d) — entitlement does not depend on any limitations period; no statutory waiting period is stated in art. 55A.053

Tex. Code Crim. Proc. art. 55A.053(b) and (c) — only one expunction on the veterans treatment court ground and only one on the mental health court ground, each requiring an affidavit attesting that the person has not previously received an expunction on that ground

A dismissal whose stated reason is not one of the five art. 55A.053(a)(2) grounds is excluded: "dismissed" alone is not enough, and the route hard-stops where the reason is not documented. LegalEase does not generate a statement that a dismissal was for want of probable cause where the order does not say so.

authority.citation: A deferred adjudication that ended in discharge and dismissal is not a dismissal for these purposes except for certain Class C matters, and is the most common misrouting in Texas; it is a hard stop rather than a warning. An informal county diversion programme not authorised under Government Code 76.011 is likewise excluded.

Tex. Code Crim. Proc. arts. 55A.251 and 55A.252 — an ex parte petition is filed in a district court for the county in which the petitioner was arrested or in which the offence was alleged to have occurred, not the county of residence; where the arrest was for a fine-only offence a justice court or municipal court of record in either county is also available. The matter is a new civil action and receives a new cause number, filed with the district clerk through eFileTexas, in person, or by mail where the clerk allows.

Tex. Code Crim. Proc. art. 55A.253 prescribes the required contents of the petition, including the petitioner's full name, sex, race, date of birth, driver's licence number, social security number and address at the time of arrest, the offence charged, the date of the alleged offence, the date of arrest, the county and any municipality of arrest, the arresting agency, the case number and court, and the list of officials, agencies, entities, central federal depositories and private compilers; art. 55A.253(b) forbids listing an agency more than once or listing divisions separately; art. 55A.253(a)(8)(C) lists private compilers separately; art. 55A.253(c) requires each district clerk to compile and maintain the agency and e-mail list on the clerk's website, and the clerk is not responsible for its completeness

Proc. art. 55A.301 — the proposed order attaches and incorporates by reference a copy of any judgment of acquittal and carries the petitioner's identifying details, the offence charged, the date of arrest, the case number and court, and the DPS incident number assigned under art. 66.251(b)(1), which in practice is the TRN from the DPS criminal history; it also requires any state agency that sent information to a central federal depository to request the return of all subject records

Timing after filing: the hearing is set not earlier than the 30th day following the date the petition is filed; the court gives a copy of the petition and notice of hearing to each listed official, agency or entity other than central federal depositories, and on receipt DPS notifies those depositories; the clerk serves by certified mail return receipt requested or by secure e-mail, electronic transmission or fax, and a state or local agency with a listed e-mail address must accept electronic service

Tex. Code Crim. Proc. art. 55A.302(c) — where entitlement would otherwise rest on the expiry of an art. 55A.052(a)(1) to (3) period without prosecutor certification, records retention is required, so waiting for limitations to run can change what the participant actually receives

Fees, read at source on 2026-08-06: art. 102.006 was repealed by S.B. 1667 effective 2025-09-01, temporarily re-added by H.B. 16 (89th Leg., 2nd C.S.) with a built-in expiry, and permanently replaced by art. 102.0061 effective 2026-01-01. Under art. 102.0061(a) a district court charges the fee applicable to filing an ex parte petition in a civil action in district court, which is the ordinary county civil filing fee and is not a flat statutory amount; under (b) a justice court or municipal court of record charges a flat $100. Article 55A.254(e) forbids any charge for electronic transmission and art. 55A.254(f) requires $25 for each listed entity unable to receive an electronic transmission, with the same structure at the order stage under art. 55A.351(b-2) and (b-3). The old $250 to $500 range is no longer reliable and is not quoted.

Tex. R. Civ. P. 145 Statement of Inability to Afford Payment of Court Costs or an Appeal Bond, approved by the Supreme Court of Texas in Misc. Docket No. 22-9090, which the clerk must make available without charge or request; art. 102.0061(d) requires waiver of the district-court fee where entitlement arises under art. 55A.053(a)(2)(A) or (B)

What the county filing figure is is not identified: art. 102.0061 resolves which provision governs but not the county amount, and whether the $25 per-non-electronic-entity charge applies twice for the same agency — once under art. 55A.254(f) and again under art. 55A.351(b-3) — is supported by the statutory text and unconfirmed in practice. Texas DPS form CR-63, Procedure for Review of Personal Criminal History Record Information: fingerprinting through the DPS FAST vendor at a $10 fingerprinting fee plus a $15 record fee, or a hard-card mail route; the DPS history supplies the TRN, the arrest date, the arresting agency and the agency list. DPS states it may oppose an expunction petition and that its legal staff cannot assist with one. The order of dismissal for each charge is obtained from the clerk of the court that dismissed the charge and is required before filing.

Self-help stop conditions on this route: state opposition or a request to retain records under art. 55A.302; mixed outcomes across charges from one arrest, governed by State v. T.S.N. and Ex parte R.P.G.P.; a felony from the same transaction; a contested limitations period or a full-versus-partial expunction question; absconding or bail-jumping history under art. 55A.154 with arts. 55A.052(a)(1) to (3) and 55A.054; an arrest on a community-supervision violation warrant under art. 42A.751(b), barred by art. 55A.153; unclear venue where arrest and alleged offence occurred in different counties; immigration consequences; wanting to attack the underlying case rather than clear it; a dismissal reason not stated on the face of the order; a completed deferred adjudication; and whether a pretrial diversion was authorised under Government Code 76.011

Texas publishes no mandatory or statewide expunction petition form; the Texas Judicial Branch forms index was confirmed on 2026-08-06 to contain no expunction form, and art. 55A.253 prescribes the contents of the petition instead. TexasLawHelp and Texas Justice Court Training Center forms are not statewide court forms and are not used.
